stem: A properly authorized Rhode Island prescriber issued a pregabalin prescription 20 days ago. A Massachusetts pharmacist can verify the prescription. Which rule is most relevant to whether it may be filled in Massachusetts?

choices.text: All out-of-state Schedule III-VI prescriptions expire after five days.
Qualifying out-of-state Schedule III-VI prescriptions may be filled within 30 days; Schedule III-V require pharmacist verification.
Out-of-state prescriptions are valid only if rewritten by a Massachusetts prescriber.
The prescription is automatically valid for one year because pregabalin is prescription-only.
Massachusetts applies the Schedule II narcotic rule to every out-of-state prescription.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts has a distinct out-of-state pathway for Schedule III through VI prescriptions. They may be filled within 30 days of issue, and Schedule III-V prescriptions require pharmacist verification.

choice_analysis.A: The five-day rule belongs to a different out-of-state Schedule II context.
choice_analysis.B: This correctly states the 30-day III-VI pathway and the verification requirement for III-V.
choice_analysis.C: The statute permits qualifying out-of-state prescriptions without mandatory rewriting by a Massachusetts prescriber.
choice_analysis.D: A general Schedule VI validity concept does not override the specific out-of-state 30-day rule; pregabalin is also Schedule V.
choice_analysis.E: Schedule-specific out-of-state rules should not be collapsed into the narcotic Schedule II pathway.

related_facts: Pregabalin is a Schedule V controlled substance.
Out-of-state prescription questions require identifying the schedule before choosing the applicable Massachusetts time limit.
explanation.mpje_trap: The prescriber’s state is not enough; schedule classification determines which Massachusetts out-of-state pathway you use.

reasoning_steps: Select the Massachusetts out-of-state III-VI pathway
